categories.name: Northcote (1907 'The Nilotic Kavirondo'), Hobley (1902, 1903) & Johnston (1902) Historical Dholuo Corpus

entries.english: Time-of-Day Birth Names Recorded by G. A. S. Northcote (1907 p. 62): Morning Sun, High Noon, Afternoon, Night
entries.translation: Onyango / Anyango (morning sun, 7–9 a.m.), Oching' / Aching' (high noon, chieng'), Odiambo / Adiambo (afternoon, 2–6 p.m.), Otieno / Atieno (night, otieno)
entries.context: G. A. S. Northcote (1907) 'The Nilotic Kavirondo', JRAI Vol. 37, p. 62

entries.english: Circumstantial & Twin Birth Names Recorded by G. A. S. Northcote (1907 p. 62)
entries.translation: Obele (born during bele 'corn in ear'), Oliech (born when an elephant liech was killed), Obonyo (born during locusts bonyo), Okach (born during famine kech), Opiyo (first-born twin), Odongo (second-born twin)
entries.pronunciation: o-be-le, o-liech, o-bo-nyo, o-kach, o-pi-yo, o-don-go
entries.context: G. A. S. Northcote (1907) 'The Nilotic Kavirondo', JRAI Vol. 37, p. 62

entries.translation: dala (homestead), chiel / ojuok (euphorbia boma hedge), rangach (main gate), simba (bachelors' hut), dero (granary)
entries.context: G. A. S. Northcote (1907) 'The Nilotic Kavirondo', pp. 58–59

entries.english: Foundational Ancestors & Migration Genealogy of the Ja-Luo (Hobley 1902 p. 27 & 1903 pp. 326–331)
entries.translation: Podho → Ramogi (Got Ramogi) → Chwanya, Jok, Omolo, Kisodhi, Gem, Kano, Sakwa, Seme, Asembo, Uyoma, Karachuonyo
entries.context: C. W. Hobley (1902) 'Eastern Uganda', p. 27 & (1903) 'Anthropological Studies in Kavirondo and Nandi', pp. 326–331

entries.english: Clan Totem & Sacred Taboo System (20 Kwero Totems in Hobley 1903 pp. 347–349)
entries.translation: kwero (clan totem/taboo: e.g., omieri python, ondiek hyena, winyo bird, rech fish, liech elephant)
entries.context: C. W. Hobley (1903) 'Anthropological Studies in Kavirondo and Nandi', JAI Vol. 33, pp. 347–349

entries.english: Supreme Sun/Sky Deity & Ancestral Spirit Veneration (Northcote 1907 p. 65 & Hobley 1903)
entries.translation: Chieng' (the Sun) / Nyasaye (Were) & tipo / juogi (ancestral spirits)
entries.context: G. A. S. Northcote (1907, p. 65) & C. W. Hobley (1903, p. 344)

source: Public Domain Historical Lexicons (Hobley 1902, 1903, Johnston 1902, Northcote 1907 & Mill-Hill Fathers 1920)
